open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: owner, through the agent
open_points.question: What concrete actor or system is the agent, through what interface does it write the connection, and on which side of the service trust boundary does it run?
options: a human-operated coding agent calls an administrative API
an automated workplace agent writes storage directly
the agent invokes an authenticated command-line operation
open_points.default_guess: an owner-directed agent calls a service administration API using a privileged credential

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: Connect an object to its folders
open_points.question: What identifies the object, and is it necessarily the same entity as the project identified by the Registry project id?
options: object and Registry project are the same entity
an object maps one-to-one to a Registry project
an object may map to multiple Registry projects
open_points.default_guess: object and Registry project are the same entity

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: a connection leaving its root folder is refused
open_points.question: What is the connection's root, how are paths canonicalized, and do symlinks, bind mounts or other indirections that resolve outside it count as leaving the root?
options: compare canonical resolved paths and reject every escape
compare normalized lexical paths only
permit resolved paths outside the root when explicitly configured
open_points.default_guess: resolve paths canonically and reject any photo or invoice folder whose resolved path is outside the configured root

witness.initial: The configured root contains a symlink named photos that resolves to a directory outside the root.
events: The agent asks to connect the object using the photos symlink.
The service validates the requested folder.
outcomes: The connection is refused because the resolved folder leaves the root.
The connection is accepted because the submitted path is lexically under the root.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed, published, settling, duplicate or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Which directory entries count as candidate photo files, which image formats are supported, and how are directories, links, non-images, corrupt images and unsupported images classified?
options: inspect every regular file and reject anything not decodable as a supported image
select files by an explicit extension and format allowlist
silently omit entries that are not recognized images
open_points.default_guess: inspect non-hidden regular files, accept an explicit decoder-backed image-format allowlist, and report every other encountered file as rejected

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: ready, placed, published, settling, duplicate or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: What does each status mean, which statuses are mutually exclusive, what transitions produce them, and how do they relate to the later result word delivered?
options: each source has exactly one current lifecycle state and delivered means published plus publication mark
statuses are independent flags and delivered means the Portal publish succeeded
duplicate and rejected are scan classifications while ready, placed and published are lifecycle states
open_points.default_guess: use one reported state per source; delivered means successfully placed, published and marked, while duplicate and rejected are terminal scan results

witness.initial: A source has been published in the Portal but the deliverer has not recorded its Portal photo id.
events: The owner asks to see what can be delivered.
The service classifies the source.
outcomes: The source is reported as published because the Portal operation succeeded.
The source is reported as placed or failed because publication is not complete until its mark is stored.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: unavailable folder is refused
open_points.question: What conditions make a folder unavailable, whether the whole project scan or only an affected subtree is refused, and what observable reason is returned?
options: any missing, unreadable or transiently failing folder refuses the whole scan
report inaccessible entries individually and continue the scan
a missing configured root refuses the scan but inaccessible descendants are individual rejections
open_points.default_guess: a missing or unreadable configured photo-folder root refuses the whole scan with a stable reason; entry-level failures are reported individually

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: a bad file is reported on its own and the others proceed
open_points.question: What makes a file bad, at which processing stages can it become bad, and what stable reason and source identity are returned for it?
options: bad means any read, decode, transform or validation failure
bad means only an undecodable image
define separate stable failure codes for read, decode, transform, validation and source-change failures
open_points.default_guess: return the source path and a stable stage-specific failure code for every file that cannot be read, decoded, normalized or validated

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: a prepared image in the Portal store, its reference and the publication body
open_points.question: What are the prepared image's encoding and quality rules, the reference format and lifetime, and the required fields and values of the publication body?
options: fix one canonical image encoding and a versioned reference/body schema
preserve any source encoding that satisfies the constraints
let the Portal adapter choose encoding and body fields
open_points.default_guess: produce a canonical JPEG with fixed orientation, metadata stripping and bounded dimensions, and return a versioned opaque reference plus a fully specified Portal request body

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: the Portal's own refusal
open_points.question: Which Portal responses count as refusal, how transport failures and timeouts are distinguished from definitive rejection, and what result the calling flow shows for each case?
options: surface the Portal status and safe response reason verbatim
map Portal and transport outcomes to stable product failure codes
treat every non-success or uncertain response as the same failure
open_points.default_guess: map definitive Portal rejections and uncertain transport failures to distinct stable failure codes while retaining safe diagnostic details

witness.initial: The calling flow sends a publish request and times out before receiving a response.
events: The Portal creates the hidden photo.
The calling flow receives no response and reports the operation result.
outcomes: The result is a Portal refusal and a retry is allowed.
The result is an unknown outcome because publication may already have succeeded.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: Place the same photo again | the first result, nothing written | none
open_points.question: What happens when the first placement is incomplete, its stored binary or record is missing, or the repeated request uses conflicting metadata for the same project and source content?
options: return the stored first result only when it is complete and valid; otherwise report corruption
repair an incomplete first placement automatically
replace the first placement with the repeated request's values
open_points.default_guess: return the original result only after verifying that the completed record and stored binary agree; otherwise fail without mutation

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions
open_points.text: same photo
open_points.question: Is sameness based on the exact source bytes, decoded pixels, normalized prepared-image bytes or another canonical representation?
options: hash exact source bytes
hash decoded oriented pixels
hash the canonical prepared image
open_points.default_guess: hash the exact source bytes within the project

witness.initial: A delivered JPEG is re-saved with identical visible pixels but different compression and metadata.
events: The replacement file becomes stable.
The owner scans and chooses it for delivery.
outcomes: It is a new photo because its source bytes changed.
It is the same photo because its decoded pixels or prepared output are identical.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions
open_points.text: the calling flow places, publishes and marks each chosen photo in that order
open_points.question: What concrete system owns the calling flow, the Portal credential and the deliverer credential, and where is the trust boundary between that system, the deliverer and the Portal?
options: the workplace kernel orchestrates both APIs and holds both credentials
a workplace backend invokes a deliverer API while a separate Portal adapter holds the Portal credential
the owner client invokes each operation directly
open_points.default_guess: the workplace kernel orchestrates the sequence and holds separate scoped credentials for the deliverer and Portal

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions
open_points.text: The calling flow records the Portal photo id at the deliverer right after publishing.
open_points.question: How does the product recover when Portal publication succeeds but the publication mark is not recorded, given that the Portal list does not return intake_id and republishing may answer 409?
options: use a Portal-supported idempotency or correlation key that returns the original photo id
provide an owner reconciliation operation that supplies the Portal photo id
record a durable publish intent and query another Portal operation that can resolve it
leave the source in a terminal manual-repair state
open_points.default_guess: persist a durable publish intent before the Portal call and require an idempotent Portal correlation mechanism that can recover the original photo id

witness.initial: A chosen source is placed and has no publication mark.
events: The calling flow publishes it and the Portal creates a hidden photo with id 81.
The calling flow stops before recording id 81.
The owner retries the delivery.
The Portal answers 409 and its photo list does not expose intake_id.
outcomes: The retry recovers id 81 and records the publication successfully.
The retry remains failed or publishes a duplicate because the original photo id cannot be determined.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions
open_points.text: A failed photo does not stop the others.
open_points.question: May deliveries for the same project or source run concurrently, and if they may, how are placement, publication and marking serialized to prevent duplicate Portal photos or conflicting marks?
options: allow only one active delivery per project
lock independently per project and source content
allow concurrency and rely on idempotency in both the deliverer and Portal
open_points.default_guess: serialize delivery per project and additionally enforce uniqueness per project and source content

witness.initial: One ready source has no placement or publication mark.
events: Two owner actions choose the source at nearly the same time.
Both flows place it and proceed to publish before either records a mark.
outcomes: Only one Portal photo is created and both flows return the same result.
Two hidden Portal photos are created or one flow fails after the other succeeds.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions
open_points.text: A change of the root or of a subfolder clears the confirmation
open_points.question: What product action changes a connection, what are its input, observable result and failures, and whether clearing confirmation and replacing the paths occur atomically?
options: extend Connect an object to its folders to create or replace a connection atomically
add a separate Change connection action
permit direct record editing and detect changes afterward
open_points.default_guess: define a separate authenticated change-connection action that atomically stores the new paths and clears confirmation

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions
open_points.text: after the owner confirms the object and its folders
open_points.question: Through what observable action and channel does the owner confirm, what exact folder identities are shown, and what evidence binds that confirmation to the record the agent writes?
options: the owner explicitly approves a rendered canonical connection summary in the workplace
the owner confirms verbally and the agent records that assertion
the owner signs a one-time confirmation token containing the project and canonical paths
open_points.default_guess: the workplace presents canonical project and folder identities and records an explicit owner approval token consumed by the agent

witness.initial: The owner has discussed two projects with similar names and two possible photo folders.
events: The owner says to use the photos folder without a machine-bound confirmation.
The agent writes one of the possible project-folder combinations.
outcomes: The record is considered owner-confirmed because the agent interpreted the conversation.
The record remains unconfirmed because no approval was bound to that exact project and canonical paths.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions
open_points.text: The agent repairs one project at a time, with a backup and the owner's permission for that project.
open_points.question: What is the repair action's input, concrete observable output, failure behavior, backup identity and restoration rule, since no primary action carries this required operation?
options: add a first-class repair-project-photo-dates action with a report and restorable backup
treat repair as an undocumented manual Portal maintenance procedure
make repair a Portal-owned operation outside this product
open_points.default_guess: add a first-class administrative action that names the project, requires bound owner authorization, creates and verifies a restorable backup, reports every changed record and makes no delivery changes on failure

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions
open_points.text: If a date still carries an offset, it stops, places and publishes nothing
open_points.question: Does one offset-bearing Portal photo block every chosen source for the project, how is an offset detected, and does a UTC Z suffix count as carrying an offset?
options: any explicit numeric offset or Z suffix on any project photo blocks the whole delivery
only non-zero numeric offsets block the whole delivery
validate only photos related to the chosen sources
open_points.default_guess: inspect every existing photo in the project and block the whole delivery only for a non-zero numeric offset, not for a canonical UTC Z suffix

witness.initial: One existing Portal photo has the timestamp 2026-11-18T10:00:00Z and a new source is ready.
events: The owner starts delivery.
The calling flow checks whether existing dates carry an offset.
outcomes: Delivery proceeds because Z denotes canonical UTC rather than an offset requiring repair.
Delivery stops because Z is an explicit UTC offset designator.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18): Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18)
open_points.text: A file is taken only after it has been unchanged for two minutes
open_points.question: Which observations must remain unchanged, when the two-minute interval begins or resets, and what happens when content changes without a detectable size or modification-time change?
options: require unchanged size, modification time and file identity across observations
require an unchanged content hash for two minutes
use the filesystem modification time alone
open_points.default_guess: require the same file identity, size, modification time and content hash at observations spanning at least two minutes

witness.initial: A file has appeared in the photo folder with a modification time older than two minutes.
events: Its bytes are replaced while preserving its size and modification time.
The service scans it.
outcomes: The file is ready because its observed metadata is unchanged.
The file is settling because its content hash changed.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18): Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18)
open_points.text: Syncthing's temporary files and hidden names, which include the phone's `.trashed-` files, are ignored
open_points.question: What exact name patterns are ignored, whether the rule applies to every path segment or only the file basename, and whether ignored directories are traversed?
options: ignore any entry when any path segment begins with a dot
ignore only documented Syncthing temporary patterns and basenames beginning with a dot
ignore hidden files but still traverse hidden directories
open_points.default_guess: do not traverse any path containing a segment beginning with a dot, and also ignore an explicit versioned list of Syncthing temporary-name patterns

events: The service recursively scans the photo folder.
outcomes: Neither file appears because a hidden directory and a hidden basename are ignored.
visible.jpg appears because only file basenames, not ancestor directories, are tested.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18): Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18)
open_points.text: The photo date comes from the camera record, otherwise from the file's modification time, and is delivered as UTC without an offset.
open_points.question: Which camera date field wins when several exist, how a camera-local time with no timezone is converted to UTC, and what exact offset-free representation is delivered?
options: prefer DateTimeOriginal and require a companion offset; otherwise fall back to modification time
interpret a timezone-less camera date in the project's configured timezone
interpret a timezone-less camera date as UTC
infer timezone from GPS or server settings
open_points.default_guess: prefer DateTimeOriginal with its explicit offset; if the camera record has no usable offset, interpret it in an owner-confirmed project timezone, convert to UTC and serialize as a specified naive UTC value

witness.initial: A JPEG has DateTimeOriginal 2026:07:01 12:00:00 with no offset, and its modification time is 2026-07-01T10:00:00Z.
events: The owner chooses the JPEG.
The service derives and publishes its photo date.
outcomes: The delivered UTC date is 12:00 because the camera value is treated as UTC.
The delivered UTC date is 10:00 because the camera value is interpreted in Europe/Madrid summer time.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18): Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18)
open_points.text: is upright and is at most 2000 px on its longest side
open_points.question: What exact resizing, color-space, animation, transparency and encoding rules determine the stored pixels and bytes?
options: define a canonical single-frame sRGB JPEG pipeline
preserve source format while applying orientation and size constraints
define format-specific canonical pipelines including transparency and animation handling
open_points.default_guess: decode one still frame, apply orientation, convert to sRGB, resize without upscaling to a 2000-pixel maximum and encode with a fixed canonical JPEG profile

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18): Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18)
open_points.text: One placement exists per project and source content
open_points.question: What uniqueness key and transaction enforce this invariant, and what happens when the same content appears at multiple source paths or filenames in one project?
options: one placement per project and byte-content hash regardless of path
one placement per project, path and content hash
one placement per project and normalized image content
open_points.default_guess: enforce a transactional unique key on Registry project id plus exact source-byte hash, regardless of source path

witness.initial: Two differently named files in separate subfolders have identical bytes.
events: The owner selects both files in one delivery.
The calling flow attempts to place each.
outcomes: Both selections return the same placement and can produce at most one publication.
Each path receives a separate placement and may be published separately.
